node.title: L1 m=4, h=3 Cartier resonance reduction
node.statement: For a hypothetical official m=4,h=3 record, choose s_nu=p-4,p-1,2,5,8 for nu=0,...,4. The Wronskian equation has the exact integrating-factor form (X^s_nu U^3D)'=X^(s_nu-1)U^2H. Formal derivatives have zero coefficient in every degree jp-1, so the former maximum deg H=4-nu is impossible. Consequently nu=4 is empty, while nu=0,1,2,3 have eliminant degree and total radical defect at most 3,2,1,0 and satisfy four printed residual coefficient constraints. In particular nu=3 is squarefree/coprime throughout. This reduces but does not close the m=4,h=3 branch or L1.
